policy: No Monroe term is treated as identical to a Nova concept by default.
Focus levels are program-specific operational labels, not universal consciousness phases.
Monroe metaphysical language is preserved as source framing and is not imported into the Nova ontology.
Only phenomenological or procedural overlap is mapped here.
A perceived vibration may map to Nova État vibratoire; generic Monroe language about vibrational energy does not automatically do so.

concepts.label: Focus 10 — mind awake, body asleep
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual, Discovery #2: Introduction to Focus 10
concepts.notes: Program-defined Focus state characterized by maintained mental alertness during deep bodily relaxation/sleep-like condition.

concepts.label: Click-out
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual, Wave I / FAQ
concepts.notes: Reported gap in immediate recall with little or no perceived passage of time; explicitly distinguished in the manual from ordinary falling asleep.

concepts.label: Kinesthetic motion cues
concepts.notes: Includes rising/falling, rocking, sliding and tipping-like sensations.

concepts.label: Perceived vibrations / electric sensations
concepts.notes: Restricted here to subjectively perceived vibration/tingling/shaking, not Monroe's broader energy vocabulary.

concepts.label: Buzzing / rushing auditory cues
concepts.notes: Auditory or head-localized buzzing is reported as one possible perceptual cue.

concepts.label: Dream-like imagery during sleep transition
concepts.notes: Images or dream-like thoughts can appear while the practitioner attempts to remain aware near sleep.

concepts.label: Release attachment to results / expectations
concepts.notes: The manuals repeatedly warn that monitoring for success or trying too hard can interfere with the process.

concepts.label: Point of Departure — 180-degree rotation
concepts.notes: A deliberate rotation technique used after establishing an expanded energy-body framework.

concepts.label: Separation / projection goal
concepts.notes: The source frames this as projecting consciousness out of phase with the physical body; that interpretation remains Monroe-specific.

concepts.label: Voluntary return to C-1
concepts.notes: The manual instructs normal breathing, opening the eyes, or finger movement as simple return cues.

concepts.label: Grounding after an exercise
source_basis: Gateway FAQ: not quite awake and alert after an exercise
concepts.notes: Includes counting, cool water, walking and other methods intended to re-establish ordinary waking orientation.

concepts.label: Experience journaling
source_basis: Gateway recommendations for use / tape-taking recommendations
concepts.notes: The manuals encourage documenting experience details and contextual variables.

mappings.basis: Focus 10 maintains mental wakefulness while the body is deeply relaxed/asleep; Nova Endormissement conscient models preserved awareness during bodily sleep onset. The units differ: Monroe describes a program state, Nova a transition/process concept.
mappings.warning: Do not encode Focus 10 = Endormissement conscient.

mappings.basis: Both involve absent immediate recall, but Monroe click-out can occur during an exercise and is explicitly distinguished from ordinary sleep; Nova Amnésie de retour concerns memory loss around return. The overlap is only mnemonic.
Rocking, sliding, tipping and rising/falling sensations overlap phenomenologically with several Nova vestibular/proprioceptive motion concepts.
mappings.warning: The manual presents a broad cue family; no one-to-one mapping is justified.

mappings.basis: Both describe subjectively perceived vibration/electric-tingling or shaking sensations in altered-state transitions.
mappings.warning: Only perceived vibrations are mapped. Monroe's general 'vibrational energy' language is excluded.

mappings.basis: Gateway describes buzzing/rushing sounds and sometimes forehead/head pressure; Nova separates generic buzzing from specifically intracranial buzzing.
mappings.warning: Localization determines which Nova node is more appropriate.

mappings.basis: Gateway discusses images and dream-like thoughts appearing while awareness approaches sleep; Nova explicitly models hypnagogic imagery and hypnagogia at sleep onset.
mappings.warning: Gateway does not require these images as a stage.

mappings.basis: Gateway repeatedly advises releasing expectations, avoiding monitoring for separation, and not trying too hard; Nova Lâcher-prise is the closest operational regulation concept.
mappings.warning: This is a practice-level similarity, not proof of identical mechanism.

mappings.basis: Gateway describes intense effort and result-monitoring as interference; this contrasts operationally with Nova Hypercontrôle.
mappings.warning: Gateway does not use the Nova term Hypercontrôle.

mappings.basis: Odyssey 3 instructs a deliberate 180-degree rotation as a technique; Nova Rotation volontaire denotes deliberately amplifying/using a rotation sensation.
mappings.warning: The surrounding Monroe energy-body theory is not imported by this mapping.

mappings.basis: The Monroe rotation exercise is intended to produce a shift/projection away from ordinary bodily localization; Nova Décrochage models the transition in point of perception.
mappings.warning: Technique goal and experienced transition must remain separate in data.

mappings.basis: Monroe's separation/projection language spans transition and outcome concepts that Nova divides into Décrochage, Sortie partielle and Sortie complète.
Both describe intentionally terminating the altered-state episode and restoring ordinary waking orientation.
mappings.warning: C-1 is Monroe terminology, not a Nova phase.

mappings.basis: Gateway grounding methods aim to restore ordinary alertness/orientation after an exercise; Nova separates post-experience anchoring and orientation concepts.
mappings.warning: Specific grounding techniques remain Monroe-source practices.

mappings.basis: Gateway recommends recording details and contextual variables; Nova Debrief structuré and Ancrage de mémoire cover adjacent post-experience functions.
source_basis: Gateway recommendations for use / tape-taking recommendations
mappings.warning: Journaling is broader than either Nova node individually.
